prompt: Order the body of the helper that makes room for one more element: do nothing if there is space, otherwise double the capacity (4 the first time), keeping the old data safe if `realloc` fails. One line does not belong.
explain: Assign `realloc`'s result to a temporary first. If it fails you get `NULL` back, and writing that straight into `v->data` would lose your only pointer to the old block. Only after the check do you store the new pointer and capacity.
